latest_rss.title: The Long March revisited: Red Army and Yi leader became sworn brothers
latest_rss.summary: More than 90 years ago, Yihai Lake in Mianning County, southwest China's Sichuan Province, became the setting for a historic encounter. In May 1935, the Red Army was making its way through areas inhabited by the Yi ethnic group during the Long March, but deep mistrust between the two sides threatened to hinder its passage. Rather than resorting to force, the Red Army sought to build trust and win the support of local Yi communities.At Yihai Lake, Red Army commander Liu Bocheng met Xiaoyedan, a local Yi leader. The two reached an alliance and became sworn brothers, helping pave the way for the Red Army to continue its journey north.Today, the historic sites where the ceremony took place remain, preserving the memory of that remarkable encounter and its enduring legacy for generations to come.
